newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Yallouz denies Brazil coffee crop forecast talk.
newsitem.headline: Yallouz denies Brazil coffee crop forecast talk.

text.p: Former U.S. Department of Agriculture forecaster turned private researcher Leon Yallouz said it was untrue that his preliminary forecast for the 1997/98 Brazil coffee crop was for either 24 million or 27 million 60-kg bags.
"There is no truth in that," Yallouz told Reuters, referring to talk circulating in the coffee market two weeks ago. "I did not publish nor reveal any crop estimate."
Yallouz has just returned from a trip to coffee fields during which he prepared his second 1997/98 crop estimate. He was previously unavailable for comment.

Since leaving the USDA last year, Yallouz has sold his research to private clients. He said he would not reveal the figure contained in the preliminary report issued to clients in January and based on field trips made in October and November.
"People pay to receive my work," he said. "If I tell the world my estimate, I will lose all my clients."
Market rumours pegged the figure at 27 million bags, then at 24 million. "That is not true either," said Yallouz, referring to the second figure.
Clients receive four reports a year from Yallouz. The second estimate would be issued at the end of February and the following one in June, he said.
"After June I will contact all my clients. If they all agree, I will then make my estimate public," Yallouz said.
The Brazilian government is currently working with a range of 18 to 20 million bags, down from an estimated 25 million bags in 1996/97.
